name: Edwin B. Forsythe National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Forty seven thousand acres of salt marsh behind Atlantic City where the eight mile wildlife drive passes eagles, ospreys and tens of thousands of snow geese in winter.
buzz: The drive at dawn is the reason to come and the observation tower is the stop; bring bug spray in summer and a scope for the far marsh.

name: The Hermitage
unique: A colonial house with a Gothic revival addition where Aaron Burr married, with original wallpaper and a story that runs from the Revolution to the Gilded Age.
buzz: The guides know the family scandals and the house is small; it is a quiet hour and the garden is free to walk.

name: Whitesbog Village
unique: A cranberry and blueberry company village in the Pine Barrens where Elizabeth White bred the first cultivated blueberry, with the packing house and workers' cottages intact.
buzz: The blueberry history is the surprise and the trails through the bogs are flat; the village is volunteer run and quiet.

name: Walt Whitman House
unique: The modest Camden row house where Whitman spent his last eight years, with his bedroom as it was and the printing press that kept him solvent.
buzz: The guides read the poems in the rooms and the house is small; it is the most personal literary site in the state.

name: Cape May Point Hawk Watch
unique: A fall migration bottleneck where thousands of hawks, falcons and eagles funnel past a platform at the tip of the cape, counted daily by volunteers.
buzz: The counters will show you what is passing and September is the peak; the platform is free and the birds come close.

name: Maurice River Kayak Trail
unique: A tidal river through the Pine Barrens with a marked water trail past osprey nests, a lighthouse and the old glassmaking town of Millville.
buzz: The water is flat and the birds are the draw; check the tide, since the river runs both ways and low tide exposes mud.

name: Branch Brook Park Cherry Blossoms
unique: The largest collection of cherry trees in a park outside Washington, 5,000 of them along a Olmsted designed boulevard, blooming for two weeks in April.
buzz: The April festival draws crowds and the rest of the year the park is a quiet Newark green space; the trees peak in the second week.

name: Tall Pines State Preserve
unique: A pine and oak forest on the site of a former golf course, with a lake, trails and a disc golf course, in a corner of Gloucester County most people drive past.
buzz: Locals use it for easy walks and the lake is good for herons; the trails are unmarked in places and the park is quiet.

name: Hoboken Terminal
unique: A 1907 ferry and rail terminal with a copper clad waiting room, stained glass and a clock tower, still handling commuters from the Hudson waterfront.
buzz: The waiting room is the room to see and it is free to walk in; the ferry dock outside is where the skyline view is best.

name: Lambertville and New Hope
unique: Twin canal towns facing each other across the Delaware, with antique shops, a 1830s mule drawn canal boat and a footbridge over the river.
buzz: The walk across the bridge and the canal towpath are the easy pleasure; weekends are busy and the shops close early.

name: Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul
unique: A granite French Gothic church with a 160 foot tower and rose windows, built by French Canadian mill workers in a mill town.
buzz: The scale is a surprise in a small city and it is free to look; it is an active parish, so avoid Mass times.

name: Nylander Museum
unique: A small museum built around the collection of a Swedish immigrant self taught naturalist, with fossils, shells and Aroostook County farm history.
buzz: The collection is old fashioned and charming and the volunteers know the county; it takes an hour.

name: Rangeley Lake
unique: A deep cold lake in the western mountains with landlocked salmon and brook trout, ringed by public land and a small resort town.
buzz: Fishermen come for the salmon in spring and the fall color is the other season; the lake is big and the wind picks up.

name: Ocean Path
unique: A flat two mile path along the granite cliffs of Acadia from Sand Beach to Otter Point, passing Thunder Hole and the pink granite ledges.
buzz: Thunder Hole is the crowded stop and Otter Cliff is the photograph; the path is easy and the waves at high tide are the show.

name: Maine State House
unique: A granite capitol designed with Charles Bulfinch, with a copper dome and a hall of flags, in a city that exists mainly to be the capital.
buzz: The dome and the chambers are the quick tour and it is free; the Maine State Museum next door is the bigger visit.

name: Camden Hills State Park
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A ridge of granite hills above Camden harbor, with trails to Mount Battie and a view of Penobscot Bay and the islands.
buzz: The Mount Battie road is the easy view and the ridge trail is the real hike; the park is popular in October.

name: Pemaquid Point Lighthouse
unique: A lighthouse on a point of folded rock ledges where the surf runs up the strata, with a fisherman's museum in the keeper's house.
buzz: The rock ledges are the photograph and the museum is small; it is on the Maine quarter and the sunrise is the local ritual.

name: Grafton Notch State Park
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A mountain pass with a gorge of potholes and waterfalls, a short trail to Screw Auger Falls and the trailheads for Old Speck and the Mahoosucs.
buzz: The falls are a five minute walk and the Table Rock trail is the view; the park is quiet compared with Acadia.

name: Mount Hope Cemetery
customer: History walkers, Stephen King readers, photographers
unique: A Victorian garden cemetery on a hill above Bangor where Hannibal Hamlin is buried and the gates and stone chapels appear in Stephen King's fiction.
buzz: King readers come for the locations and historians come for the Civil War generals; the self guided map is at the gate.

name: Kennebec River Rail Trail
unique: A paved trail along the Kennebec from Gardiner to Augusta, past shipyards, a paper mill and the river where the state's shipbuilding began.
buzz: The Bath waterfront and the river views are the reason to ride; the trail is flat and connects to downtown Bath.

name: Rocky Gap State Park
unique: A lake in a gap of the Allegheny Mountains with a sandy beach, a lodge and trails up to rocky overlooks, just off Interstate 68.
buzz: The lake swim is the summer draw and the canyon trail is the hike; the lodge and casino make it a weekend base.

name: William Paca House
customer: Gardeners, history people, house tour fans
unique: A Georgian mansion with a two acre pleasure garden restored to its 1765 plan, hidden behind a Annapolis street.
buzz: The garden is the surprise and the guided tour explains the signer's life; the house is small and the tour runs on the hour.

name: Oregon Ridge Nature Center
unique: A nature center on a wooded ridge with live owls and hawks, a lake and trails, plus a summer concert series in the hollow.
buzz: The birds and the easy trails are good with children and it is free; the July Fourth concert is the local tradition.

name: Annmarie Sculpture Garden
unique: A wooded path of outdoor sculpture in a county park, with a gallery, a children's garden and a program of artist residencies.
buzz: The sculpture walk is the reason to come and the fairy houses in the woods are the family surprise; it is small and cheap.

name: Fair Hill Natural Resources Area
unique: Five thousand acres of rolling fields and woods on the Delaware line, with horse trails, a steeplechase course and fox hunting country.
buzz: The spring and fall race meets are the local event and the trails are quiet; the fields are open and the ticks are real.

name: Harriet Tubman Museum and Educational Center
unique: A community museum in downtown Cambridge with Tubman's story, local African American history and the murals that led to the larger state park.
buzz: The volunteers are descendants and local historians and the museum is small; it pairs with the Tubman visitor center 15 miles away.

name: Monocacy National Battlefield
unique: The battlefield that saved Washington in 1864, with a walking trail along the Monocacy, a restored farmhouse and earthworks.
buzz: The ranger talks explain why a small battle mattered and the loop trail is easy; it is free and rarely crowded.

name: Spruce Forest Artisan Village
unique: A cluster of log cabins and a church beside a covered bridge where working artisans demonstrate pottery, weaving and woodwork.
buzz: The artisans are the reason to stop and the covered bridge is the photograph; it is small and the drive through the Casselman valley is beautiful.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park
unique: Sixteen thousand acres of river valley inside the Baltimore beltway, with a swinging bridge, the ruins of a 19th century mill town and trails along the Patapsco.
buzz: The swinging bridge and the Avalon ruins are the walk; the park is busy on weekends and the river floods after storms.

name: Brookside Gardens
unique: Fifty acres of display gardens with a conservatory, a rose garden and a Japanese tea house, free and open every day.
buzz: The conservatory is the winter visit and the butterfly exhibit in summer is the family draw; it is free and rarely crowded on weekdays.
